description: Huntington Beach; Pure touches the sand for the first time; the coding class; the closing narration. Incorporates Sequence 7 (The Lesson) as beats 6.07-6.08. Source breakdown: scenes/sequence_06_the_sand_breakdown.md (8 film beats, 1:41).
_comment: The film's only exterior sequence. s06_02_touch is the title payoff and the highest-polish beat in the film -- see RENDER_STYLE.md on shifting the CA dissolve focus_center_frac onto the hand rather than the face for the sand insert.

beats.note: First coastal exterior in the film. The three of them small against the water. After five sequences of interiors, this is the film breathing out.

beats.display_name: 6.01 The family walks to the sand

beats.note: "I grew up ten miles from this."
Slow but not precious. The moment should feel actual, not symbolic.
Not ceremonially -- he just kneels down, the way you would if you wanted to feel something.

beats.display_name: 6.02 Insert: the hand in the sand
beats.note: HIGHEST-POLISH FRAME IN THE FILM. Light the sand so texture reads in black-and-white. Apply the CA dissolve gently here with the focus centre on the hand, not the face.
Takes a handful. Lets some fall. Holds the rest. Stays there a moment of actual presence, then the hand relaxes and the rest falls.
Three words, after the silence of the action. Let the words and the image sit together -- do not rush to the next beat.

beats.display_name: 6.03 Medium wide -- all three, equal weight
beats.note: The film's only peaceful family image. Static, held. No one looming, no one at the edge.

beats.display_name: 6.03 Pure rises; the others come alongside

beats.note: No gesture, no embrace, no dialogue. They're just at a beach looking at water. That's the point.
Deliberately rhymes with the prison library (2.07): a small room, a few computers, someone learning because code gives them what they can't get elsewhere. Pure is now on the other side of that.

beats.display_name: 6.04 V.O. 'It's yours if you want it.'
beats.note: "I started a free coding class. Nothing formal. Just -- here's what I know. It's yours if you want it."
Genuine, unselfconscious. The kid means it as a simple question -- the weight is what Pure brings to it.

beats.display_name: 6.05 Cut to Pure -- the only cut here

beats.note: Don't fill it. Let it breathe. He already knows this answer.

beats.display_name: 6.06 The first unguarded smile in the film
beats.note: Small and real, not cinematic. A man who has finally stopped managing his presentation.

beats.display_name: 6.06 'I didn't make it. I came back.'
beats.note: "I didn't make it. I came back. That's the only thing that matters." The film's thesis, delivered casually, to a child. The understatement is the point.

beats.display_name: 6.07 Slow pull back from the beach
beats.note: One of the film's few camera movements -- pushes are for emphasis, this pull-back is for release. Ends wider than the film started.
"...love isn't a subscription... It's the sand under your feet -- the ground you've been standing on your whole life. You just never looked down."
"His mother didn't need him to be successful. She needed him to be present."
"His brother didn't need him to be perfect. He needed him to be real."
"Love yourself. Love others. Anything can happen." The fade begins on this line.

beats.display_name: 6.08 Fade to black -- do not cut
beats.note: Fade, never cut. Completes in silence. The final sensation is wide, then black, then nothing.
End of NO SAND BEACH. Sequence 7 (The Lesson) is folded into beats 6.07-6.08 above.
